analysis.title: How Close Is Europe To Another "Whatever It Takes" Moment? Goldman Builds A Fragmentation Alarm To Find Out
key_insights: Goldman economists Sven Jari Stehn and Giovanni Pierdomenico built a Euro Area Fragmentation Risk index to predict when the ECB will be forced to intervene in bond markets. The index currently points to limited fragmentation risk despite the recent widening in French spreads.

Spread levels alone are an unreliable guide. Spreads above roughly 250bp have often been associated with ECB intervention (2010-2012, 2020, 2022), but Italy in 2018 exceeded those levels without prompting intervention.

Across seven major past interventions, the GDP-weighted 10Y spread averaged about 250bp at intervention, about 300bp debt-weighted and 350bp+ in the worst-hit countries, with significant variation between episodes.

Spread dispersion and volatility spike notably around ECB interventions. Current dispersion (about 0.02 standard deviations vs a 0.35-0.4 mean at past interventions) and volatility (about 0.03 vs about 0.16) are low, so the French selloff is orderly.

In Goldman's logit models scored on precision-recall, spread volatility (rolling standard deviation of the 10Y spread) was the best predictor, spread levels second (spreads over Bunds beat spreads over swaps), and dispersion third. Bank spreads and the euro ranked near the bottom.

The index combines seven indicators: 10Y spread volatility, 90th percentile 10Y spread, change in the 10Y spread vs its trailing one-year median, cross-country dispersion of 10Y and 2Y yields, bid-ask spreads, and senior bank spreads over Bunds. Weights follow predictive accuracy, with volatility about a quarter of the index.

The ECB has usually intervened when the index moved 1.5-2 standard deviations above its average. The index averaged about 2.7 standard deviations in prior interventions (about 2.6 before the TPI announcement) and was a hair above zero as of Oct. 2. It has risen about half a standard deviation since end-2025, driven by volatility and spread widening.
The index had the best hit rate for predicting interventions versus plain spreads and the ECB's SovCISS, though Goldman concedes the difference in forecasting power is quantitatively limited.

Goldman's caveat: identifying the fragmentation risk that would prompt intervention is difficult. Disorderly dynamics are easier to capture than judging whether they are fundamentally deserved, which requires views on the macro, fiscal and political backdrop.

TPI use is limited to unwarranted, disorderly market dynamics and eligibility depends on compliance with the EU fiscal framework and sustainable debt. The article argues France (5%+ deficit, fragile budget process, Sep 18 downgrade, unrest) would struggle to argue its widening is unwarranted.

French 10Y spread over Bunds broke back above 150bp on Tuesday, closing at 153bp (up 5bp) after touching 157bp intraday. The Oct. 2 high of 159.2bp is the level to watch. French 10Y yield was 4.92%, a few bp below the 2002 highs hit earlier in October.

French 10Y yields rose 16bp on Monday Oct 19, the biggest one-day jump since March 2025, after weekend protests and curfews in riot-hit cities. Goldman's rates desk noted OATs underperformed (10y +13bp).

Contagion is contained so far: the Italian BTP-Bund spread was 1bp wider at 112bp (touched 119bp), and EUR option volumes are more than 30% off their highs. Goldman's FX desk notes this as a French rather than euro-area episode.
Money markets price 23bp of ECB tightening by year-end and 71bp by end-2027, so the market is not pricing a dovish rescue.

The article's own view: the index measures panic, not solvency. An orderly grind wider in French spreads never trips the alarm and keeps raising France's interest bill. The next test is Lagarde's Wiesbaden speech on Wednesday and a break of the 159bp Oct. 2 high, which would bring loud ECB monetization talk.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's index is near zero, well below the 1.5-2 standard deviation intervention zone, with orderly French selling, low volatility and dispersion, and contained contagion (BTP-Bund at 112bp, EUR option volumes 30% off highs). Fragmentation risk is limited.
tension_points.bear_case: The index fires only after volatility and dispersion explode, so a steady, orderly grind wider in French spreads never trips it or qualifies as unwarranted for TPI, while France's deficit, downgrade and unrest raise the interest bill. Low fragmentation risk is not the same as low risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The OAT-Bund spread taking out the 159bp Oct. 2 high, which the article expects would bring loud ECB monetization chatter.
